title: Indian Art and Culture: Temples, Stupas, Dances, and Music

questions.question: A hemispherical Buddhist relic mound encircled by a path for clockwise circumambulation is a:
questions.rationale: The stupa (e.g. Sanchi) holds relics under its anda dome; a chaitya is a prayer hall and a vihara a monastery.

questions.question: The Kailasa temple at Ellora, carved top-down out of a single rock, was built under which dynasty?
questions.rationale: Rashtrakuta king Krishna I commissioned the Kailasa temple in the 8th century — the largest monolithic excavation in the world.

questions.question: Which feature belongs to the NAGARA temple style?
options: Curvilinear shikhara with amalaka and kalasha
questions.rationale: Nagara (north Indian) temples — like Khajuraho or Konark — have beehive-curved shikharas crowned by amalaka and kalasha; gopurams/tanks are Dravida, star plans are Vesara.

questions.question: The Brihadeshvara temple at Thanjavur, hallmark of Dravida architecture, was built by:
questions.rationale: Rajaraja I (c. 1010 CE) raised the Brihadeshvara (Rajarajeshvaram) — a 66 m vimana in granite — at the height of Chola power.

questions.question: The Greco-Roman influenced school of sculpture, with wavy-haired Buddhas in grey schist, is:
questions.rationale: Gandhara (northwest, 1st–5th c. CE) blended Hellenistic realism with Buddhist subjects; Mathura worked in spotted red sandstone.

questions.question: Which dance is correctly matched with its state?
questions.rationale: Kathakali is Kerala's green-faced dance-drama; Bharatanatyam belongs to Tamil Nadu, Odissi to Odisha, Kuchipudi to Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: The classical grammar of Indian drama and dance — mudras, karanas, and rasa theory — was codified in:
questions.rationale: Bharata's Natya Shastra (c. 200 BCE–200 CE), the 'fifth Veda', defines 108 karanas and the aesthetic theory of rasa underlying all classical performing arts.

questions.question: The Sattriya dance tradition, recognised as a classical dance in 2000, grew out of the satras founded by:
questions.rationale: The 15th–16th century saint Sankardeva created Sattriya as part of his neo-Vaishnavite satra monasteries in Assam.

questions.question: The Carnatic music trinity consists of:
options: Purandara Dasa, Kanaka Dasa, Swati Tirunal
Bhimsen Joshi, Bismillah Khan, Ravi Shankar
questions.rationale: The trinity of Tiruvarur — Tyagaraja, Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri (18th–19th c.) — defined the kriti repertoire of Carnatic music.

questions.question: The serene Gupta-era Buddha delivering his first sermon, in dharma-chakra-pravartana mudra, is the masterwork of:
questions.rationale: The Sarnath Buddha — transparent drapery, full serenity, preaching gesture — is the summit of Gupta classicism in stone.
